lessons.title: HS Codes and Import Duties for Machinery
lessons.body:
Every machine you import has an HS codeâa six- to ten-digit number that tells customs what it is and how much duty you pay. For small Chinese machines like brick makers, maize grinders, or sewing machines, codes usually start with 84 (mechanical appliances) or 85 (electrical). For example, a diesel engine falls under HS 8408.90, while a sewing machine is HS 8452.10. Get the code wrong and you risk overpaying, underpaying (with penalties), or having your goods seized.

To find your code, use the World Customs Organization's HS database or your country's customs tariff book. In Nigeria, use the Nigeria Customs Service Trade Portal; in Kenya, the Kenya Revenue Authority iTax system. Ask your Chinese supplier for the HS code they useâbut verify it yourself. Check the duty rate: many African countries charge 5â20% import duty on machinery, plus 0â35% excise duty on some items, and 7.5â18% VAT. For example, Ghana charges 5% duty on most industrial machines, plus 12.5% VAT and 0.5% ECOWAS levy.

Duty is calculated on CIF value: Cost of goods + Insurance + Freight. If your machine costs $2,000, insurance $50, and freight $300, CIF = $2,350. At 10% duty, you pay $235. Always ask for the correct HS code before shipping. If unsure, hire a customs broker to classify your goodsâcosts $50â$200 but saves thousands in fines.

Keep a record of the HS code on your commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading. Mismatched codes cause delays. Use online tools like TariffData or DutyCalculator to estimate total landed cost. Remember: duty rates change, so check annually. For small machines, many countries offer reduced rates under the AfCFTA if you meet rules of originâbut that requires proof the machine is made in Africa, which Chinese imports do not qualify for.

lessons.title: Pre-Shipment Verification of Conformity (PVoC) and SONCAP
lessons.body:
Before your machine leaves China, it must pass a conformity check called PVoC (Pre-Shipment Verification of Conformity) or SONCAP (Standards Organisation of Nigeria Conformity Assessment Programme). Without it, your goods will be rejected at the port. PVoC is required in Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and others; SONCAP is Nigeria's version. The goal is to stop unsafe or substandard products.

How it works: You hire an accredited inspection company like SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek, or Cotecna. They inspect the machine at the factory or warehouse in China, test it against local standards, and issue a Certificate of Conformity (CoC). For SONCAP, you need a Product Certificate first, then a SONCAP Certificate per shipment. Costs: $300â$800 per shipment, depending on machine value. The process takes 5â10 days. You must provide the supplier's test reports, ISO certificates, and a proforma invoice.

If you skip PVoC, your goods arrive without a CoC. Customs will flag them, and you'll pay a penalty (15% of CIF) plus re-inspection fees. In Nigeria, without SONCAP, goods are seized and you may need to re-export at your own cost. In Kenya, PVoC is mandatory; non-compliant goods are destroyed or returned.

To avoid trouble: Tell your supplier you need PVoC/SONCAP before shipping. Book inspection early. Ensure the machine has a nameplate with model, voltage, and power. If the machine is second-hand, many countries ban it outrightâcheck first. For small Chinese machines, buy from suppliers who already have experience with African PVoC. Ask for a sample CoC from a previous shipment. Keep digital copies of all certificates. Your customs broker will need them to clear goods.

lessons.title: Sea Freight vs. Air Freight: Cost and Time
lessons.body:
Sea freight is cheap but slow; air freight is fast but expensive. For small Chinese machines, sea freight is usually the only practical option because machines are heavy and bulky. A 20-foot container from Shanghai to Mombasa costs $1,500â$3,000 and takes 25â40 days. Air freight from Guangzhou to Lagos costs $4â$8 per kg and takes 3â7 days. A 100 kg machine by air would cost $400â$800; by sea, maybe $150â$300 but wait a month.

Sea freight options: FCL (Full Container Load) means you rent the whole container. LCL (Less than Container Load) means you share with othersâcheaper for small volumes but slower (add 7â14 days for consolidation) and higher risk of damage. For a single small machine, LCL is fine. For 5+ machines, compare FCL. Always get quotes from freight forwarders like DHL Global Forwarding, Kuehne+Nagel, or local African forwarders. Ask for all-in cost: ocean freight, terminal handling, documentation, and customs brokerage.

Air freight is best for urgent spare parts or very high-value, low-weight items. But for a 200 kg brick maker, air freight could cost more than the machine. Also, air freight has weight and size limitsâcheck with the airline. Some forwarders offer air-sea combination (sea to Dubai, then air to Africa) but it's rarely worth it.

Key tip: Never choose the cheapest sea freight without checking transit time and reliability. Some cheap carriers transship multiple times, causing delays. Use a forwarder with a proven track record on your route. For landlocked countries like Uganda or Rwanda, add trucking from Mombasa or Dar es Salaamâanother $1,000â$2,500 and 5â10 days. Always insure your shipment; sea freight insurance costs 0.5â1% of CIF value.

lessons.title: Customs Clearance: Documentation and Agents
lessons.body:
Customs clearance is where most importers lose money and time. You need a complete document set: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading (B/L), certificate of origin, PVoC/SONCAP certificate, and import declaration (IDF in Kenya, Form M in Nigeria). Missing one document can delay your goods for weeks.

The commercial invoice must show seller and buyer details, HS code, description, quantity, unit price, total value, and Incoterms (FOB, CIF, etc.). The packing list shows how goods are packed, weights, and dimensions. The bill of lading is your title to the goodsâwithout it, you cannot collect cargo. Always request a telex release or original B/L from your supplier. For sea freight, the B/L arrives after the ship; for air freight, use an air waybill (AWB).

Hire a licensed customs agent (broker). In Nigeria, use a licensed agent from the Nigeria Customs Service; in Kenya, a clearing agent registered with KRA. A good agent knows the local system, can classify your goods correctly, and fast-tracks clearance. Expect to pay $200â$500 per shipment for brokerage, plus government fees. Ask for a breakdown: customs duty, VAT, levies, terminal charges, and agent fee. Never pay cash without a receipt.

Use the customs portal to track your declaration. In Kenya, use the Kenya TradeNet System; in Nigeria, the NICIS II. If you import regularly, consider getting a customs bond or a deferment account to pay duties monthly. For small machines, many countries have a simplified clearance for low-value shipments (under $1,000), but you still need documents. Always keep copies of everything for 5 yearsâcustoms can audit later.

lessons.title: Understanding VAT and Other Taxes
lessons.body:
VAT (Value Added Tax) is a consumption tax you pay on imports. In most African countries, VAT is 15â18% of CIF value plus duty. For example, if CIF is $2,350 and duty is $235, VAT is calculated on $2,585. At 16% (Kenya), VAT = $413.60. In Nigeria, VAT is 7.5%, so $193.88. Some countries charge VAT on the duty-inclusive value, others on CIF onlyâcheck your local rules.

Other taxes and levies: ECOWAS levy (0.5% of CIF) in West Africa, East African Community levy (0.5% of CIF) in EAC, and various port levies. In Ghana, there's an African Union levy (0.2%) and a COVID-19 levy (1%). In Kenya, there's a Railway Development Levy (1.5% of CIF) and an Import Declaration Fee (2% of CIF, minimum KES 5,000). These add up. Always ask your broker for a full tax computation before you commit.

Can you avoid VAT? Only if you are VAT-registered and can claim input credit. For a small business, you may not be registered. But if you sell machines, you should registerâthen you can offset import VAT against VAT you charge customers. Keep all import documents; they are proof for input credit. Some countries exempt certain machinery from VAT if used for agriculture or manufacturing. For example, Kenya exempts VAT on solar equipment and some agricultural machinery. Check the VAT Act or ask customs.

Never undervalue your goods to reduce VAT. Customs uses valuation databases and can penalize you 2â5 times the duty. If you think the value is wrong, appeal with evidence (invoices, bank transfers). Pay all taxes through the official portalânever cash to an agent. Get an electronic receipt. For small machines, total taxes can add 20â40% to your landed cost, so budget for it.

lessons.title: Avoiding Demurrage and Port Delays
lessons.body:
Demurrage is the fee you pay when your container sits at the port beyond free time. Free time is typically 3â7 days for sea freight. After that, charges start at $50â$150 per day per container, rising daily. In Lagos or Mombasa, demurrage can quickly exceed the value of your machine. Port delays happen due to missing documents, customs queries, unpaid duties, or slow inspection.

To avoid demurrage: Start clearance before the ship arrives. Send all documents to your agent 7 days before ETA. Pre-pay duties and taxes so customs can release immediately. Ensure your PVoC/SONCAP certificate is ready. If customs asks for inspection, be present or have your agent push for same-day inspection. Use a reputable agent who knows the port officials. In Nigeria, demurrage at Apapa Port can be $100/day after 5 free days. In Kenya, Mombasa charges $80/day after 7 days.

Other port delays: Terminal handling charges (THC) must be paid before cargo release. In some ports, you need a gate pass and a delivery order. For landlocked countries, your container may sit at the port of entry waiting for transit documents. Always clear transit bonds in advance. If you have multiple containers, clear them one by oneâdon't wait for all.

If demurrage starts, negotiate. Some shipping lines waive part if you have a good reason (e.g., customs strike). But don't rely on it. The best strategy is speed: have your agent on standby, pay all fees online, and collect your goods the same day they are released. Consider using a bonded warehouse if you cannot clear immediatelyâcosts $10â$20 per day but cheaper than demurrage. For small machines, always budget an extra $200â$500 for port delays. Never leave your container at the port; it's the fastest way to lose money.

quiz.q: What does HS code stand for?
quiz.explanation: HS code is the international Harmonized System for classifying traded products.

quiz.q: Which of these is a typical HS code for a small diesel engine?
quiz.explanation: HS 8408.90 covers compression-ignition internal combustion piston engines (diesel).

quiz.q: Duty is calculated on which value?
quiz.explanation: Customs duty is typically assessed on Cost, Insurance, and Freight (CIF) value.

quiz.q: If CIF is $2,000 and duty rate is 10%, how much duty do you pay?
What is PVoC?
quiz.explanation: PVoC stands for Pre-Shipment Verification of Conformity, required in many African countries.

quiz.q: Which organization issues SONCAP certificates?
quiz.explanation: Accredited inspection companies like SGS, Intertek, and Cotecna issue SONCAP certificates.

quiz.q: What happens if you import goods without PVoC in Kenya?
options: A) Goods are destroyed or returned
B) You pay a small fine
quiz.explanation: In Kenya, non-compliant goods without PVoC are destroyed or returned at importer's cost.

quiz.q: How much does a typical PVoC inspection cost?
quiz.explanation: PVoC inspection costs range from $300 to $800 per shipment.

quiz.q: Which is generally cheaper for heavy machines?
quiz.explanation: Sea freight is much cheaper for heavy, bulky items like machines.

quiz.q: What does LCL stand for in shipping?
quiz.explanation: LCL means Less than Container Load, where you share container space.

quiz.q: Approximately how long does sea freight take from Shanghai to Mombasa?
quiz.explanation: Sea freight from Shanghai to Mombasa typically takes 25â40 days.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of air freight per kg from China to Africa?
quiz.explanation: Air freight from China to Africa costs about $4â$8 per kg.

quiz.q: Which document is your title to the goods?
quiz.explanation: The bill of lading is a document of title that allows you to claim the goods.

quiz.q: What is an IDF in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: IDF stands for Import Declaration Form, required for customs clearance in Kenya.

quiz.q: What is Form M in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Form M is Nigeria's import declaration form for customs.

quiz.q: How much does a customs broker typically charge per shipment?
quiz.explanation: Customs brokerage fees range from $200 to $500 per shipment.

quiz.q: What is the VAT rate in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's VAT rate is 7.5%.

quiz.q: VAT on imports is usually calculated on which amount?
quiz.explanation: VAT is typically calculated on CIF value plus customs duty.

quiz.q: Which of these is an additional levy in West Africa?
quiz.explanation: ECOWAS levy is charged on imports in West African countries.

quiz.q: Can you claim input VAT credit if you are VAT-registered?
quiz.explanation: VAT-registered businesses can claim input VAT credit on imports.

quiz.q: What is demurrage?
options: A) A fee for late container pickup
quiz.explanation: Demurrage is a penalty fee for keeping containers at the port beyond free time.

quiz.q: How many free days do you typically get before demurrage starts?
quiz.explanation: Most ports offer 3â7 days of free time before demurrage charges begin.

quiz.q: What is the best way to avoid demurrage?
options: A) Pay all duties early and have documents ready
quiz.explanation: Paying duties early and having complete documents speeds clearance and avoids demurrage.

quiz.q: What is a bonded warehouse used for?
options: A) Storing goods before duty payment
quiz.explanation: A bonded warehouse stores goods before customs duty is paid.

quiz.q: Which document shows how goods are packed?
quiz.explanation: The packing list details how goods are packed, including weights and dimensions.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a certificate of origin?
options: A) To prove where goods were made
quiz.explanation: A certificate of origin proves the country where goods were manufactured.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common inspection company for PVoC?
quiz.explanation: SGS is one of the accredited companies for PVoC inspections.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of sea freight insurance?
quiz.explanation: Sea freight insurance typically costs 0.5â1% of CIF value.

quiz.q: Which system is used for customs declaration in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Kenya uses the Kenya TradeNet System for customs declarations.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for undervaluing goods to reduce VAT?
quiz.explanation: Customs can penalize undervaluation by 2â5 times the duty owed.
